about: What the code before the figure service did with the comparison's spectrum overlay (the track stage's [data-stage-canvas="overlay"] and Δ pane [data-stage-canvas="diff"]), recorded from that code itself before it went: never hand-computed, and not to be made again. Replayed by src/test/figureOverlayCases.test.ts (every section) and python-backend/test_figure_overlay_cases.py (the `r7` cases' `expected.py`). Values: a number, or "nan" / "inf" / "-inf" (pick_cases.json's way). Pointer places are CSS px from the pane's plot frame's top left; `view` records the painted axes (x, y ends), the frame (box) and the scale (px per natural-log unit across, px per dB up), the new read contract's inputs. An index is the point's place in the line's every point (scene `lines.<id>.xs`). `changes_with` names the spec change or design rule that changes the case; its `expected` is still the old answer.

spectrum.about: The base group's median (3 recordings), the compared recording, one track with no role, and the Δ (compare − median). Each line's full data is held whole (localLine); levelBins as the backend sends them, so the old R6 order puts the loudest first and the quietest on top.

r7.description: A narrow peak of the compared line 6 px left of the pointer, near its top: the point nearest within 20 px is the peak.

The pointer exactly halfway (20 px each) between the compared line and the median at one bin: equal distance. The old path reads the line first in plot.lines, which is the draw order (R6: loudest first), so the compared line wins.
r7.changes_note: Spec change 1 fixes the draw order (base group, median, compare 1, ...), and the pick must not depend on it: a tie goes to the line declared first (docs/figure-design.md 第 9 節: 同じ距離の点).

r7.description: No point within 20 px (both lines 40 px away, vertically): the line nearest in height at the pointer's column is read; the two are equally far, and the old path reads the first in draw order (compare).
r7.changes_note: The tie under the pointer follows plot.lines (the R6 order) in the old path.

r7.description: No point within 20 px, low on the plot: the point under the pointer of the line nearest in height (the track with no role, the quietest).
The pointer 2 px into the plot, before the lines' first point (22.4 Hz, ~10 px in) and far from every line in height: over none of them, nothing is read.
The pointer before the first point but within 20 px of the compared line's first point: the old path reads it (the radius search is not limited to the line's extent).
The pointer past the lines' last point (16.3 kHz), far from every line: nothing is read.
The pointer in the compared line's NaN run (bins 32-39), at its level: no compared point to read; the median, the nearest in height at the column, is read.
The pointer on the median's silent stretch (−300 dB, bins 44-47, drawn as a gap): silence is no value; another line is read.

The level axis zoomed to its lower half: the compared line's peak is above the top. A pointer at the top edge over the peak does not pick it (off screen); it reads the point nearest it on screen within 20 px or, with none, the line under the pointer, its mark held at the edge.

The level axis zoomed to its lower half, the pointer high at a bin where only the compared line is near in height but above the top: the line under the pointer nearest in height is read, a value past the axis read at the plot's edge.
From the compared line's point at bin 20, → three times and ← once: one full-resolution point each, along the line read.
From the compared line's last point before its NaN run (bin 31), →: the next point with a value (bin 40), the run skipped.
From the median's point before its silent stretch (bin 43), →: the next point with a value (bin 48), silence skipped.
From the lines' last point (bin 58), →: nothing further (the data's end).
Zoomed across (30-50 % of the axis): from the last bin inside the window's right edge, → reads nothing (past the plot's side), though the data goes on (bin 29).
Zoomed across: from the first bin inside the window's left edge, ← reads nothing (past the plot's side) (bin 18).
The Δ pane: the pointer 4 px above a point of the Δ line: that point.
The Δ pane: the pointer in the Δ's NaN run (bins 32-39, longer than the pick window): answered, no value (`empty`).
The Δ pane: from bin 30, → twice (over the NaN run to bin 40) and ← once.

r9.description: The frequency axis whole: the fields write its stated limits as painted.
The level axis whole: the fields write the R9 dB range (rounded to 5/10/20/25 dB steps).
Zoomed across (30-50 %): the window's ends are made at the field's decimals (fieldWindow) and the fields write them exactly.
The level axis zoomed to its lower half: the fields write its painted ends.
Typed 123.456789 – 4567.891234 Hz across (fractional input): the window set and the ends painted after.
Only the minimum typed (100 Hz), the maximum left as shown: that end keeps its place.
The minimum typed (1000 Hz) and the maximum cleared (blank: that end automatic, the axis's own).
Applied as shown on a zoomed axis: the window is the one it was.
Typed past the axis's limits (5 Hz – 50 kHz): the window is clamped to the whole axis.
Typed minimum above the maximum: the popover keeps open with its error, no window set.

r13.description: A press that stays put: a click, acted on at once.

A double click on the overlay: the first press clicks, the second (detail 2) takes it back, and the dblclick resets the zoom. The reset fires twice: the lanes' surface (attached first, as attachStageGestures does) answers the second press with its own selector, which is not the overlay, so it resets the clicked plot too (plotInteraction.ts:418).
A slow double click (700 ms apart) that the browser still counts as one (detail 2): the arbitration reads no clock, so it is the same as a quick one.
Two clicks the browser counts as single (detail 1 each): two clicks, nothing taken back, no reset.

A click on the overlay, then the second press of a double click on the Δ pane: the overlay's click is taken back and the overlay's zoom reset (the second press is the double click wherever it lands); the Δ pane's dblclick resets its own too.
A click on the overlay, then a double click's second press on a track lane (another surface): the overlay's click is taken back and its zoom reset.
A click on the overlay, then the second press lands off every plot (the page's body): still taken back, the overlay's zoom reset.

A click on the overlay, a click on the Δ pane, then a second press (detail 2) on the overlay: only the press right before is a double click's first; the Δ pane's click (the last) is taken back, the overlay's stays.
A press dragged past the threshold and let go: a box zoom, no click.
A press moved within the drag threshold (3 px) and let go: a click, at the release's place.
A click on the overlay, then a drag on the Δ pane: the click is no longer current (a waiting one would not be done), nothing taken back.
A press whose release is lost (the next move has no button): told as no click (not current), its action never done.
A dblclick on the plot with no click to take back: the zoom resets.

pending_click.description: The figure's own tap (attachStageGestures): a click on a spectrum line, its read in or waited for, acts on nothing; the overlay's click only leaves a trigger's event line out (toggleEvent).
A click while the compared line's full data is on its way: once it is in, the click is done once, on the read at the press.
Every line held whole (nothing to wait for): the click is done at once.

Not done: a press on another plot (the Δ pane) before the read is in takes the click's place (current() false). The Δ pane's own click, on a line held whole, is done at once (the one entry in `acted`).
